A nonparametric measure of dependence for mixed types of data, known as Kendall's tau, is particularly useful for analyzing categorical data, including the ordering of different categories. Building upon earlier contributions by Aggarwala and Goo (1989) and Chaudhuri and Frankel (1992), this research develops an efficient estimator for estimating Kendall's tau in the presence of mixed data types. The proposed estimator has been found to be asymptotically normal and weakly efficient for handling nominal data, while also being able to process both nominal and ordinal data, thus providing an adaptive approach to data analysis. To facilitate practical applications, the paper presents simulations and a real-world data example to validate the efficacy of the proposed estimator.

The number of connected devices, such as vehicles, is rapidly increasing, driving demand for advanced and efficient IoT services, particularly edge intelligence technology, which facilitates smart decision-making at the edge through deep learning. However, concerns over user privacy persist, threatening to hinder the adoption of edge intelligence and IoT technologies. To address these challenges, this research outlines a framework for implementing privacy-preserving edge intelligence in vehicular networks, leveraging blockchain technology to rectify data inaccuracies from moving vehicles. A specific protocol is proposed to safeguard user data during edge inference, involving a collaborative proof mechanism to verify user data integrity without compromising their privacy. A concrete scenario involving vehicle lane-assistance and traffic management is simulated to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed framework, comparing it with traditional methods like Google's AutoML and CNN-MLP models. Furthermore, this paper offers practical guidelines for deploying blockchain technology to enable private and reliable edge intelligence services in vehicular networks.

This study focuses on the Euler characteristic surface of a (p,q)-linked cycle pair consisting of two cycles with q and p edges respectively. By applying the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, a formula for the Euler characteristic surface can be derived, which reveals that its degree corresponds to the total number of invariants for the (p,q)-linked cycle pair in the family. We provide a detailed computation for the elementary invariants using the cutting and sliding operations, resulting in a specific computation scheme for the Euler characteristic surface. Notably, the Euler characteristic polynomial for any (p,q)-linked cycle pair is divisible by the Chevalley polynomial, a defining characteristic of braids, to the power of q-2. Furthermore, the Euler characteristic polynomial for any (p,q)-linked cycle pair is also divisible by the braid polynomial sigma to the power of q-3. Experimental results for the 2-component case show that the Euler characteristic polynomial behaves similarly to the Alexander polynomial in terms of link data, being a multiple of the first power of the Alexander polynomial. We also demonstrate how to express the Euler characteristic polynomial as a linear combination of the basis polynomials in the Alexander module.

Our analysis focuses on an adjusted predator-prey model based on Holling-Tanner's equations, which incorporates a strong Allee effect into the prey population growth rate. We establish stability conditions for both positive coexistence equilibrium points as well as trivial equilibrium points related to predation and prey populations. The investigation also involves conducting numerical simulations, which reveal a range of dynamic behaviors in the continuous model, including oscillations, limits cycles, and other patterns of movement, as well as analyzing the evolution of the prey population over time. Additionally, we discuss corresponding changes in the discrete model, which arises from discretizing the continuous equations using the forward Euler method and comparing it with the actual numerical solution of the continuous model.

The Hirsch Conjecture was a theory claiming that a d-dimensional polytope with n faces cannot exceed a diameter of n - d. This assumption was disputed by Santos, whose findings led to the conclusion that there is no upper limit to the Hirsch distance. Concurrently, employing the ellipsoid volume lead to an exponential worst-case bound for the facet pivot simplex method was achieved. Our study aims to surpass this by deriving an iteration bound of $O(n^{\omega(d)-1}d)$, thereby building upon earlier work by Combettes et al. Our new bound is obtained by utilizing combinatorial properties inherent to the Hirsch distance, thereby bridging the concepts of the ellipsoid method and the facet pivot simplex method.

We explore in an associative ring R with identity, the scission group NK1^{gr}(R), formed by the graded version of Niu-enk's unitary group. Our study includes key properties of this group in relation to ring homomorphisms, specifically with Gr(R) and Q(R) via the pinnings p: U_{2n} -> GL_n. Additionally, we establish how Nk_1^{gr}(R) partitions the set of units in Q(R) into equivalence classes based on p. The concept of pointed K-theory is introduced as pinning's image, which serves as a subcategory of the units' conjugation classes, which is then linked to the units' conjugation classes of the ring's graded unitary K-theory. The concept of R's weak relative K_1 is introduced, which is established as the quotient p'(NQ_1(R)/pinning's image), and this is then applied to the Graded and Rationalised cases, which are explored in section 3.

This paper undertakes a thorough comparison of the comprehensive NLO computation by Mellinger and Stirling, which incorporates the full off-shell $t\bar{t}$ dynamics, with an approximate on-shell calculation in the context of a study aimed at top quark physics. We then assess how utilizing the four-momentum of an intermediate $t\bar{t}$ pair reconstructed from $p_{t_1}+p_{t_2}+p_{p_{W}}$ influences the measurement of the $W$ boson mass in a $W$ boson constrained analysis. Utilizing the EXCIRI software, which allows for a detailed, event-by-event evaluation of NLO and approximated on-shell computations, we simulate various $W$ boson mass measurements across various bins of the $p_{\mathrm{T}}^{l}$ and $p_{\mathrm{T}}^{E_{\mathrm{T}}^{\mathrm{miss}}}$, and examine how these measurements are impacted when using the four-momentum of an intermediate $t\bar{t}$ pair, while maintaining all other analysis aspects. Our investigation reveals that off-shell effects can have a significant impact on four-momentum choices and certain observables in $W$ boson mass measurements, leading to deviations of up to 7 MeV in these measurements.

The susceptibility of facial recognition systems to deceptive attacks limits their practical use in real-world scenarios. As a result, researchers have been working to develop robust countermeasures for detecting fraudulent attempts. Our study delves into the potential of using a Vision Transformer-based model for on-the-fly identification of spoofed faces in a zero-shot setting. We test the performance of this approach with three publicly available datasets, revealing that the transformer-based model surpasses a traditional CNN-based model in terms of accuracy. Furthermore, we assess various access control methods, revealing that a hybrid approach combining the transformer model with a conventional CNN-based model yields optimal results.

Deep reinforcement learning's (DRNL) potential in autonomous driving is significant, however, it's still a relatively new area and research is still ongoing. In order to assess its feasibility, a new framework is proposed that integrates DRNL strategies. This framework aims to answer three crucial questions: how to formulate a driving task within DRNL, how to design an effective reward system, and what kind of DRNL algorithm is best suited for autonomous driving. By addressing these key points, researchers can develop more realistic and safe driving policies. This paper presents an overview of the proposed framework and discusses future avenues for exploration.

Evolutionary algorithms have seen significant advancements through the integration of parallel processing over the past decade, enabling improvements in algorithmic efficiency and performance by distributing fitness evaluations across multiple processors. However, implementing a synchronous evaluation scheme in evolutionary algorithms poses difficulties, primarily due to issues such as load imbalance and, more critically, evaluation time bias. The latter occurs when the algorithm's selection processes wait for all functional evaluations to complete before the next generation of operations begins, resulting in slower processors becoming a bottleneck. To address this problem, we have developed a novel frequency-based parent selection strategy within the framework of an asynchronous evolutionary algorithm, specifically tailored to mitigate evaluation time bias. Through numerical experiments conducted on a problem set designed to induce evaluation time bias and an extended variant of a well-known benchmark problem, we have demonstrated the efficacy of our proposed strategy in reducing the adverse effects of evaluation time bias and enhancing the performance of the algorithm compared to conventional approaches such as random and best rules.

The recent microlensing event, microlensing light curves, are sensitive to the light source's brightness and color as well as the lensing effect. A recent analysis of the microlensing event OGLE-2017-BLG-1434 detected a sub-saturn mass planet, which confirmed previous results from a NIRKeck AO. A new analysis of the microlensing event using the H-band data and a more accurate lensing light curve model, found the planet mass ratio to be in the range of 0.0033 to 0.0039, which is consistent with the previous results from the NIRKeck AO. A new analysis of the microlensing event also updated the cold super-Earth mass range to 3.4-5.8 M⊕, which provides further evidence for the existence of such planets. The concept of an effective, time-independent generator has been developed for certain types of dynamic systems by filtering out the rapid oscillations. Systems with periodic coefficients and high-frequency components can be approximated by their frequency-modified counterparts. Research on closed quantum systems revealed that the approximation's accuracy scales quadratically with the expansion's parameter. Building upon this theory, we examine how this applies to weakly driven open quantum systems governed by a specific type of equation. By expanding the system's dynamics, we can identify the dominant terms, as well as complex and less-intuitive correction terms. Notably, these effects are not limited to the system's eigenstates, as evidenced by our theoretical findings. Our study also highlights the order at which various phenomena, such as high-frequency oscillations, virtual heating, dissipation-related corrections, and drift states, occur. Our results were validated through precise numerical simulations of a spin chain in contact with bosonic baths. These corrections have significant implications for understanding the thermalization of closed quantum systems. Moreover, they may become experimentally significant in the near future. Our analysis further sheds light on the occurrence of virtual cooling in the absence of dissipative terms at a specific order. These discoveries expand upon the current understanding of how dissipation-related corrections affect the behavior of quantum systems.

Our recent studies of the effects of Rh on CePD$_{1-x}$D$_{1-x}$ revealed a swift
change in magnetic properties as rhodium concentration was increased. Neutron
depolarization began at very low rhodium concentrations while simultaneous
quenching of long-range magnetic order occurred. Through detailed analysis of
neutron data and comparisons with our existing knowledge of the material's
magnetic behavior, we determined that neutron depolarization was a result of
interference with the Ce $4f$ magnetic moment by the Krinovalh lattice's
magnetization. We found that neutron depolarization can be used to identify the
presence of magnetic phases in a material, in our experiment corresponding to
a static phase of Ce-based magnetic moment. We observed depolarization rates
consistent with those predicted due to magnetic scattering in our experiments.

A massive star-forming area, G176.51+00.20, located 6.5 kiloparsecs away, is home to numerous high-mass stars and an estimated 10 to 30 solar masses of dust. Utilizing the 21-cm Hydrogen line, we observed self-absorption phenomena in 11 spectral lines. These absorptions, characterized by an excess column density, exhibit a wide range of durations and depths. A notable correlation exists between the observed depth and line center frequency, indicative of a non-thermal origin, specifically dust. A single event, however, could be attributed to a dense molecular cloud blocking a dense HI cloud. A notable absorber with a duration of 2.62 kilohertz shows significant variability, possibly due to a high-mass star's influence or future molecular cloud collapse. These absorbers hold the potential to be utilized as backlights for studying dust properties in this heavily obscured star-forming area.

We demonstrate the topological equivalence of all intermediate beta-transformations with a specific type of greedy beta-transformation that incorporates a hole at zero. By employing this equivalence, we obtain a detailed characterization of these transformations, yielding new insights and results in various areas, such as Krieger embeddings, survivor sets, Hausdorff dimensions, bifurcation sets, and badly approximable numbers. We show that certain classes of sets associated with these beta-transformations possess unique properties, specifically that they are winning in Schmidt games and have the countable intersection property.

Determining the CP-violating phase phi_s resulting from mixing-induced phenomena in Bs decays is a crucial method for discovering potential new physics phenomena. Utilizing approximately 15.6 fb^-1 of data, we conducted an analysis of CP-violating phi_s, utilizing its occurrence in exclusive pi+ pi- final states that involve a J/psi meson, a process theoretically predicted by the flavor-changing b->s transition. Our measurements of phi_s in the integrated pi+ pi- signal revealed no occurrence of CP-violating phi_s, with a best-fit result of 0.2° and an associated 95% confidence interval of -3.8° to -3.8°. This corresponds to a sin phi_s value of -0.01 ± 0.36.

It is evident that deep neural networks excel in extracting relevant features from a given dataset, but they may not necessarily excel in adapting these features to datasets with different underlying characteristics. The transfer learning process, particularly domain adaptation, involves adjusting data from a source domain with labeled data to match the characteristics of a target domain with fewer or no labeled data. In this research paper, the primary focus lies on the domain adaptation problem, with an in-depth evaluation of various deep neural network techniques performed through multiple cross-image classification experiments.

In this note, we compute exact counts for subsets of $\mathbb F_q^2$ that contain no three points that are collinear. For any field $\mathbb F_q$, and for any $n$ points $(x, f(x))$ where $x$ varies over an $n$-element subset $A$ of $\mathbb F_q$, we determine the exact number of $k$-tuples that are mutually collinear for all $3 \le k \le n$. Our results for three collinear points allow us to derive asymptotic bounds for the maximum number of arcs in $\mathbb F_q$.

A pictorial proof shows that there are $\binom{n+2}{4}$ equilateral triangles in an equilateral triangle with side length n, divided into unit triangles, by utilizing a pictorial demonstration that dividing the triangles into four equal parts and repeatedly halving the size of the parts results in 1$\frac{n+1}{2}$ equal parts, where this is understood to be either a whole number or a mixed number.

Despite recent advancements in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), explaining their predictive results remains an underdeveloped area in the research community, which is particularly concerning given the potential risks of making critical decisions based on unverified predictions in real-world applications. To address this issue, existing research has primarily focused on offering post-hoc explanations offering local insight into individual predictions. To bridge this gap, we propose the development of a more comprehensive explanation framework, which enables the creation of global explanations for GNNs, and furthermore allows us to address the limited understanding of how GNNs function with different graph data. To achieve this goal, we introduce the ParamExplainer, a novel explanation framework based on counterfactual reasoning, which enables us to answer three essential questions: (1) what specific changes are required to make a certain prediction, (2) what specific changes are needed to make certain features relevant to the prediction, and (3) what specific changes are needed to make certain nodes/edges relevant to the prediction. To validate the effectiveness of ParamExplainer's post-hoc explanations in providing meaningful insights into GNN behavior, we conduct an empirical study on various benchmark datasets with diverse graph structures. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide valuable understanding of GNNs' behavior on both synthetic and real-world graph datasets.

The peculiar system, RXCJ0232.2-4420, is composed of a massive cluster and a nearby Compton bright galaxy group.  Recent studies have revealed that the cluster and galaxy group share a common origin.  The current analysis aims to identify any substructures within the cluster, by examining X-ray data collected by the Chandra observatory at a significant depth of 12.6 keV-ks. The observations indicate that the cluster, at z=0.235, comprises two distinct components separated by approximately 1.5'. The brighter, western component correlates with a massive galaxy residing at the system's core, exhibiting properties indicative of shock features. The eastern component, exhibiting lower surface brightness, houses four galaxies clustered closely, observed to undergo collisions with each other and also undergoing a collision with the core component. The colliding substructures are separated by significantly less than 0.2 Mpc. The colliding substructures' velocities, estimated to be approximately 1500-2000 km s$^{-1}$ relative, are comparable to that of the system as a whole. The current analysis implies that this cluster, at least in its present state, is undergoing significant reconfiguration due to ongoing substructure interactions.

Recently, the Legendre Memory Unit (LMU), a novel type of recurrent neural network (RNN), has garnered significant interest due to its ability to outperform traditional RNNs, including Gated RNNs and Long Short-Term Memory, on various recency regression benchmarks. Notably, LMU has demonstrated an exceptional capacity for learning both long- and short-term sequences. Despite LMU's superior performance, a key limitation remains - training LMU is computationally intensive, with previous attempts to utilize GPU parallelism yielding only marginal speedups. To address this, a new parallelization method for LMU has been developed, which aims to resolve two major obstacles to parallel training: the sharing of memory parameters and the variable output shapes of masked sequence prefixes. To overcome these challenges, an innovative memory partitioning scheme and a new output concatenation method have been designed, enabling efficient parallel training of LMU on modern GPU architectures. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of this approach, showcasing significant speedups on both single- and multi-GPU setups, with a single-GPU implementation yielding a speedup of 3.2X over the standard sequential implementation, and an 8-GPU setup yielding a speedup of 22.8X over a previous parallelization attempt.

Our primary focus is on exploring particle physics beyond the Standard Model by detecting particles with extremely weak interactions. Given the vastness of the parameter space involved and the absence of a clear theoretical framework, our approach involves employing a wide range of methods to investigate feeblely interacting particles. In this article, we review the current progress in this field and the strategies being used in experiments, emphasizing the importance of top-down and bottom-up approaches in the search for new, invisible particles.

The development of a shared language is crucial for effective cooperation between individuals, yet it poses a challenge for migration. This challenge arises because moving between regions of differing languages often results in a significant language barrier. However, it has been observed that successful communication can still occur even when a significant number of individuals with different languages reside within the same area. This suggests that a personal naming strategy is at work. In this study, we investigate the personal strategy in a simplified model and discover that it promotes shared languages with high levels of internal consistency and is capable of withstanding the effects of movement and random changes. Interestingly, we also find that this level of coherence occurs with relatively few requirements, leading to predictable outcomes when individuals occasionally randomly change their language, such as limited predictability and the potential for personal strategies to survive in a world where individuals occasionally randomly change their language.

PINN algorithms have been adapted for solving time-dependent partial differential equations by including an additional equation that represents the partial derivative with respect to time. The incorporation of this extra equation presents challenges, particularly when dealing with time-dependent problems due to initial conditions. Due to these challenges, researchers have developed methods that utilize PDE data without relying on initial or boundary conditions. These studies, however, primarily focused on one-step methods and did not thoroughly examine how these methods perform on long-time problems where the solution depends heavily on the starting point. As a result, one-step methods are likely to have limited applicability to real-world problems that often require predictions over extended time periods. As an initial attempt to address these limitations, we conducted experiments on one-dimensional heat equation with known solutions. The experiments revealed that one-step methods are highly sensitive to spectral bias and are unable to accurately capture solutions over long time periods due to this limitation. Interestingly, we discovered that introducing a momentum term into the one-step method can significantly reduce the impact of spectral bias, thereby improving predictions significantly.

We examine a two-wave system in the interval (-1,1), where one wave absorbs energy and the other does not, with partial damping applied. We show long-term stability under long-term local dissipation, where the rate of energy loss is proportional to $|\omega|^{\kappa}$ for frequencies with high values, where $0<\kappa<\frac{1}{2}$. This result improves the general stability threshold in the literature to $k>\frac{3}{2}$. The proof relies on frequency analysis building on previous work in frequency domain by Kim and Popescu for similar systems without coupling, where $k$ is the point where the dissipation operator changes from zero to a positive constant.

Recent advancements in deep reinforcement learning have led to widespread success across various applications, yet deep RL methods struggle with transparency and clarity in understanding and explaining their learned models. This has prompted the development of highly interpretable, symbolic approaches using induction algorithms in artificial intelligence. Despite the advancements in deep RL, there is a gap in designing efficient and usable symbols through traditional induction methods. This research introduces a novel induced logic learning algorithm and applies it to integrated Markov decision processes (IMDPs) for building hierarchical reinforcement learning frameworks (HHRLs). By leveraging a novel induction method, our approach develops efficient symbols for IMDPs to create hierarchical policies in complex tasks. This allows the creation of hierarchical policies for highly sophisticated robotic control tasks, and our experimental results show that HHRLs outperform hierarchical baseline methods in tasks such as making a coffee and assembling a laptop. Moreover, our approach offers a balanced combination of learning efficiency and high task performance.

We've developed an all-optical technique for optically isolating single-photon sources without using quantum measurement. By combining classical optical isolation with a specific non-linear process, we're able to increase vulnerability of photons traveling in one direction while decreasing it for photons traveling in the opposite direction. We've achieved a measured $4$ dB photon number system size increase, equivalent to a 6-photon Fock state system size increase, all without using photon detection. We've also demonstrated a 29.5 dB system size increase in single-photon system compatibility with fiber-optic networks, equivalent to the loss of 9 photons in reverse direction. We've calculated potential outcomes for various levels of initial system non-classicality, showing that using an 8-photon Fock state could lead to a 10-photon system size increase forward and 19-photon Fock state equivalent compatibility with quantum networks.

We investigate a variational problem of minimizing a specific functional defined as the supremum difference between a function and its transformed version with a sum of translated components, within the space of functions having a limited derivative. Under a condition on dimension, it's proven that this problem can be relaxed without loss of optimality. Our study leverages a sharp inequality initially discovered by Gaudin in 1989 to yield a solution, and as a byproduct, it recovers an alternative derivation of a variant of the unimodalization problem with sparsity control initially solved in 2017.

The CRESST experiment is the world's most sensitive detector of Dark Matter (DM) based on $^7$Ge direct detection using the spin-dependent (SD) interaction, thanks to its large amount of $^6$Li produced by neutron activation. CRESST's sensitivity for DM mass ranges from 1 MeV to 10 MeV and 100 MeV to GeV reaches close to or surpasses past experiments, while competing with xenon-based direct detection experiments in a larger mass range from 10 to 100 MeV for DM cross sections as low as $10^{-41}$ cm$^2$.

Blind Image deblurring attempts to estimate a latent image's sharpness and a blurred image, an ill-posed problem solved by restricting solutions to 'regular' options. Researchers have developed multiple strategies to solve this problem, including the blind image deblurring one. Our approach utilizes the fact that most images can be represented as a combination of basic image components. Based on this understanding, a new blurring model has been developed that uses the blurring coefficient from the image, not just the original one. An innovative optimization technique called alternating direction multipliers has been introduced to solve the objective function derived from this. Our results outperform previous methods, and we've also found that the model is efficient and able to handle different image types effectively.

This paper introduces a new approach to the associative Baker-Ahlfors equation with cohomological relevance and demonstrates that a specific simplified form mirrors the geometry-adapted Yang-Baxter equation concept. Furthermore, the study includes multiple examples to illustrate this theoretical framework.

Formal verification using Hoare logic is a widely established technique for establishing software correctness through formal specifications, though it demands extensive manual input due to the discrepancy between technical code and natural language descriptions.  This paper introduces an enhanced version of Hoare logic that is formalized within the extended second-order classical logic framework.  Leveraging recent advancements in second-order logic formalization and natural language understanding, we propose a formal verification framework capable of translating natural language assertions into Hoare logic formulas, thus streamlining the process of formal verification.  Experimental outcomes validate the feasibility of deriving correct formal specifications from natural language inputs, paving the way for automated formal verification in software engineering.

Distributed consensus is crucial for various distributed systems, such as distributed databases and blockchain systems, to function correctly. The Canopus algorithm has shown great promise in addressing this challenge, particularly for permissioned blockchain networks, by efficiently handling blockchain growth, minimizing storage and communication requirements, and ensuring leadership is fair, while guaranteeing safety and liveness. The main drawback of Canopus, however, is that it does not protect the system from failures or attacks initiated by untrustworthy network participants. In this research, we propose RCanopus, a new algorithm that overcomes this limitation by enabling Canopus to tolerate failures, including both unexpected system failures and malicious actions, without having to identify which participants are trustworthy in advance. The experimental results show that RCanopus offers significant performance improvements over other permissioned blockchain algorithms, including HotStuff, with a 1.5 to 2 times faster throughput, and also outperforms other fault-tolerant algorithms, such as Zyzzyva, by 1.5 to 2 times.

Recent studies have challenged our understanding of the role that cholesterol plays in lipid bilayers, particularly when in contact with water. We investigated the elastic properties of pure cholesterol monohydrate micelles in the smectic phase, as well as lipid bilayers composed of dipalmitoyl cholesterol and dipalmitoyl cardiolipin, using atomic force microscopy. By analyzing indentation data through a finite element method, our results showed no significant alteration to the bending modulus of cardiolipin bilayers upon adding cholesterol. We propose that in scenarios such as this, where hydrophilic heads and cholesterol are interconnected, conventional lipid models may not yield the most accurate bending modulus measurements. Cardiolipin's exceptionally high cholesterol affinity was also examined, in an effort to measure the binding constant.

This paper examines the loop quantum cosmological model derived from the ADM Hamiltonian, looking at scenarios where matter is incorporated into the model. Loop quantum cosmology is a crucial component of the current research into the quantum properties of the universe. By applying canonical quantization and introducing discrete eigenvalues for geometric operators within this model, the fundamental equations of the model can be solved and key equations can be simplified and analyzed. Numerical solutions of the resulting equations reveal that the model predicts a "quantum bounce," in which the universe avoids the big bang singularity due to the discrete properties of space. The critical point at which this "quantum bounce," occurs depends on the matter incorporated into the model, and the universe properties at the beginning of the big bang are dictated by a quantum gravitational length scale.

The Pierre Auger Observatory catalog details 100 extensive air-showers 
recorded between 2004 and 2020 for high-energy particles exceeding 95% 
confidence, which exceeded the energy of $10^{20}$ eV. This comprehensive catalog 
provides an extensive amount of data on these high-energy events, encompassing 
a comprehensive set of parameters for each complete data set. A comparative 
analysis is conducted with an equivalent catalog from the High-Rigidity 
Explorer experiment. A statistical examination reveals that 82 events from the 
catalog satisfy specific criteria for being authentic signals originating from 
extraterrestrial sources. A subsequent review of existing high-energy cosmic ray 
phenomenon theories is performed.

Incorporating deep detection models into practical applications requires accurately estimating their uncertainty levels.
This study proposes a Bayesian uncertainty estimation module, referred to as BayesOD, which can be integrated into existing object detection models to facilitate uncertainty calculation.
Utilizing Monte Carlo sampling from neural network weights, BayesOD generates uncertainty metrics for object prediction distributions.
This technique can be combined with any object detection model, and we demonstrate its effectiveness by adapting it to Faster R-CNN to calculate total uncertainty for object detection tasks.
This study provides an uncertainty estimation method that can be universally applied, and our numerical and visual evaluations confirm its accuracy.

The traffic forecasting task has been a significant research area for quite some time. Recent advancements in deep learning have led to the development of models that produce accurate traffic predictions. However, existing studies tend to use traffic data from fixed locations, which may not be suitable for dynamic scenarios. To address this limitation, we introduce a new forecasting approach that can handle changing traffic conditions and dynamic camera placements. By representing traffic data as a sequence from continuous movie clips, we can capture the evolving nature of traffic conditions over time and space. To handle this dynamic data type, we introduce Traffic Moving Snippets (TMS), a new framework that can process sequence-based traffic conditions. Additionally, we create two artificial datasets based on real-world scenarios and evaluate state-of-the-art forecasting models, including CNN and Transformer models, to predict dynamic traffic conditions.

In recent years, rewriting theory has been applied to solve problems in category theory. This research expands on the concept of rewriting by incorporating Gray categories. A key challenge arises when extending the rewriting method, as it requires a form of coherence between match and mismatch rules. Surprisingly, this coherence is automatically satisfied in the context of 2-categories, but fails to hold in higher dimensions naturally. To address this issue, we introduce the notion of "rewriting with context" and show how it applies to 2-categories, 2-theories, and 2-universal rewriting, showcasing its significance in 2-category theory. Furthermore, we explore an extension of this framework to n-categories and show how Gray-rewriting contributes to coherence theory. Specifically, we prove that a particular extension of strict n-categories allows for more flexibility, potentially providing a solution to the problem of free development in higher categories.

Automatic hippocampus segmentation on magnetic resonance imaging is a crucial operation, particularly for patients suffering from Alzheimer's and epilepsy, where tracking changes over time and comparing scans with clinical data is often necessary to assess treatment effectiveness and disease progression. Current deep learning-based methods primarily employ one network to address all cases, including healthy and patient scans, which often lead to subpar results due to the significant differences in these images. A more effective solution involves training separate networks optimized for specific image types: healthy scans, epilepsy scans, and dementia scans. Each model is then fine-tuned on its respective category and collectively used in a study involving 1,250 subjects spanning a wide range of conditions and scan types.

We scrutinize an experiment claiming to showcase the quantum pigeonhole effect by violating the classical principle of locality. The experiment in question utilized two interferometers with shared paths and detected a paradoxical outcome where two particles on the same path lacked any form of classical coincidence, the so-called "pigeonhole effect." We analyze the issue by introducing two transversal modes into each interferometer, the 'up' and 'down' modes, in conjunction with existing mode types, the 'left' and 'right' modes. Utilizing the quantum statistical theory based on the positive-operator-valued measure framework, we demonstrate the violation of the classical coincidence condition. Moreover, we show the viability of the quantum pigeonhole effect under specific detection scenarios and investigate the pivotal detection condition for overseeing the effect. We also emphasize the necessity of incorporating the weak interaction to detect quantum effects within this experiment.

Our research involved simulating the low-earth-orbit radiation environment for cosmic-ray antiprotons using a low-energy Monte Carlo model. We calculated and analyzed the spatial distribution of trapped antiprotons in quadrupole and Gridded Vane Potential System models, finding significant trapping areas in the $-X$ region. We also investigated the relationship between magnetic field strength and $z$ axis length in examining the effects of these regions on low-energy cosmic-ray antiproton trapping.

A network's expressivity is a crucial factor in assessing deep neural networks, but this concept is especially important for graph neural networks, given their inherent cyclic structure. To address the expressivity limitation of existing graph neural networks, we've developed an innovative pyramid-like deep graph neural network architecture that features multiple levels of shrinking skeleton and links between graph components. This enhanced graph neural network was thoroughly evaluated through experiments on standard benchmark datasets, resulting in superior performance compared to existing methods. Notably, the proposed model achieved state-of-the-art results on Cora, CitCiteseer, and PubMed datasets, with its flexibility allowing it to effectively combine various graph neural network components, such as GCN, GraphSAGE, attention mechanisms, and GAT modules.

To achieve differential privacy in low-rank matrix completion, we introduce the private huber mechanism, a modification of the random Gaussian noise mechanism. This new mechanism surpasses the previous best performance, particularly in scenarios with small noise parameters where it avoids overflow errors. The Huber mechanism's noise level is determined by a specific formula based on the problem's constraints, and its effectiveness is validated through numerical experiments in matrix completion. These tests demonstrate the superiority of the huber mechanism in scenarios with varying noise parameters and data noise levels. Furthermore, theoretical analysis and simulations confirm the private huber solution's ability to converge to its non-private counterpart, while also exhibiting similar statistical properties to the non-private solution in such cases.

We propose a novel approach to modeling interstellar dust by combining two processes: electrons on large dust grains and the outgassing of small particles. The PAH (polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon) emission from these small particles is observed and included in this method, along with data on the extinction and polarization of starlight. An analytical framework involving a single parameter is developed to describe these phenomena, and this approach is tested using a series of reddening data from various astronomical sources. The results indicate that this combined model accurately describes the extinction and polarization of starlight in the diffuse interstellar medium, and the parameters of this approach are suitable for future use in cosmological simulations.

The 13 Myr-old CIDA 1 star CIDA 1, which has a mass of approximately 0.11 solar masses, exhibits protoplanial disk activity, indicating a higher mass than expected. Research has discovered an edge-on disk with a large-scale structure, which is likely caused by a massive planet's influence. By analyzing VLT/SPHERE images, it was possible to model the planet that orbits CIDA 1, which has a mass of around 1.5-2.5 Jupiter masses. The outer structure of the disk, which is located 10-15 stellar radii away from the star, may be affected by the presence of this planet, which is located closer, at 4-5 stellar radii away. The presence of this planet challenges the traditional "core accretion" model of giant planet formation, which is unexpected for a low-mass star.

Consider the Lights Out game played on a simple undirected graph, G. This game begins with all vertices in an 'on' state. A click on a vertex $v$ toggles its own state, as well as the states of its adjacent vertices. The objective of the Most Clicks problem is to find a sequence of clicks that toggles all vertices to an 'off' state, prioritizing sequences requiring the most clicks. This research demonstrates that, except when G is bipartite, such optimal sequences exist. Additionally, we present a polynomial-time algorithm for identifying these optimal sequences in bipartite graphs.

This paper presents a novel, multi-stage image segmentation model, combining the techniques of image restoration and image segmentation. The integration of image restoration components enables the proposed model to effectively handle images corrupted by noise, blur, missing data, and colorization tasks. Notably, our model demonstrates superior colorization capabilities, producing high-quality results even on colorless 3DXL camera images. Additionally, our model achieves state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy on SIUVDS, Oxford, and GTK datasets, with comparable performance to SOTAs on the CamVid dataset, outperforming it by a margin of 2.1% and 2.4% for classes A and B respectively.

Program analysis through Abstract Interpretation involves simulating real program behavior using mathematical abstractions, ensuring the results are precise yet computationally feasible. A major challenge arises due to infinity loops during analysis, so techniques are employed to force termination by artificially stopping the ascending phase and then adjusting the derived information during the downward phase to correct any inaccuracies. However, traditionally, the transition between these phases has been seamless, failing to account for diverse termination strategies in the ascending phase. This paper introduces the Decoupling Algorithm, which aims to differentiate these phases, offering greater flexibility and efficiency in handling various termination strategies without compromising result accuracy.

Our research demonstrates that topological phonons presence depends on the structural symmetry and chemical composition, allowing non-uniform illumination to manipulate oxide perovskites phononic bands into a desired configuration. Utilizing classical molecular dynamics and first-principles calculations, we observed that a monochromatic light source can induce a light-induced symmetry breaking, while ultrafast pulsed illumination can temporarily convert a phononic crystal into a topological phase. Our findings offer an innovative approach for managing mechanical phonon signals via light, potentially enabling the development of advanced phononic devices based on oxide perovskites.

Unsupervised outlier detection in various fields has seen the rise of general methods based on the k-nearest neighbor algorithm. However, these methods have a drawback, their computational complexity grows quadratically with the size of the dataset, making them unsuitable for large datasets. Our proposed solution fast-trio involves adapting the triplet proximity graph proposed by Deng et al. to facilitate the search for a nearest neighbor. By integrating this graph with outlier scoring, we demonstrate the effectiveness of fast-trio by reducing the time needed to compute outlier scores while maintaining precise results. Our solution is available at https://github.com/vaswanirohit/fast-trio.

The probability amplitude for an electron to be excited by interacting with a thin mirror moving at non-relativistic speeds is calculated, and it is observed that this probability depends on the direction of the electron's magnetic dipole moment and its velocity. Consequently, when the electron decays, it can emit photons with polarizations independent of its magnetic dipole moment's orientation. Furthermore, it is shown that two photons can be emitted through a process where a virtual photon reflects off the thin mirror, creating correlations in the photon spins.

When training graph representation learning models, we often utilize an underlying graph structure to accelerate matrix computations, yet these models can produce unfair node embeddings, leading to biased node representations and unfair outcomes. To address this issue, we've developed a new approach that incorporates neighborhood fairness directly into the node embedding learning process by localizing fairness constraints to each node's 1-step neighbors, thereby enabling efficient learning. Our framework, as a first of its kind, enables joint node embedding and outcome prediction and can accommodate various outcome distribution and fairness constraint definitions. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, which prioritizes fairness without compromising accuracy, yielding results comparable to state-of-the-art methods.

This research focuses on kinetic models for reversible enzyme reactions and evaluates the effectiveness of two analytical techniques in obtaining solutions up to the third level of approximation. We apply the method of successive iterations and a recent iterative adsorption distribution approach, deriving the corresponding probability functions for molecular configurations. Furthermore, our analysis yields equations governing the reaction's progress over time and enzyme product distribution dynamics. The obtained results facilitate comparisons with existing literature, enabling us to determine various reaction-related parameters.

The results of an experiment involving the Large Hadron Collider are presented, where proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV are examined to investigate the production of supersymmetric particles above 13 TeV. Using 2016 data from 13.6 inverse femtobarns, researchers searched for signs of these particles in configurations with either one or multiple jets and also with indicators of an imbalance in transverse momentum. Based on this investigation, 95% confidence level exclusions were made of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of simplified models of

We introduce the concept of a rational expectation financial bubble, characterized by its finite duration marked by a stochastic, mean-reverting termination point. To identify and analyze such bubbles in financial markets, we utilize a statistical tool, expecting certain patterns and anomalies in price data outside of the equilibrium state. To our knowledge, our proposed diagnostics are novel and innovative, and can be universally applied across different financial markets and models of bubble formation, as long as they meet the basic criteria mentioned earlier. When testing for different types of financial bubble models, our diagnostic tool proves effective and, interestingly, even a straightforward stochastic termination times can produce complex behaviors resembling chaos, fractals, and extreme price fluctuations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a simple bubble model can effectively capture the unique characteristics of asset price time series, such as the one displayed by digital currencies, while also explaining other prevalent financial phenomena, like volatility clustering and the long-term dependence in price movements.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed in their ground state with either constant driving forces or time-varey oscillatory inputs. Calculations included key metrics such as energy levels, position, momentum, and their rates of change. Since one of the characteristics of Monte Carlo simulations involves sampling at fixed time intervals, the short-time behavior couldn't be directly determined. To overcome this limitation, the authors applied a technique that used multiple sampled data points to yield a time-resolved information, effectively making the simulations suitable for driving signals with a high Fourier component frequency. An alternative method was proposed to determine the short-time behavior by using a Taylor series expansion, effectively making the simulations suitable for driving signals with a high Fourier component frequency. Another technique was proposed to determine the short-time behavior by using the underlying stochastic equation. The authors compared the outcomes of these methods and found them to be in good agreement.

Recent research has shown significant progress in using reviews for making recommendations, with methods that generally fall into two categories: analyzing reviews independently and combining them with users' past behavior. To improve recommendations, we have developed a new approach, the Sentiment-aware Interactive Fusion Network (SIFN), that effectively integrates reviews with users' historical behavior through a two-part process. In the first part, called the Evaluator, a BERT-based model is used to learn a comprehensive representation of users' past purchases based on their implicit feedback and the reviews' sentiment. In the second part, the Analyser takes these learned representations along with the item's description and user profile to make accurate predictions. By doing so, SIFN is able to capture how users feel about items they have previously bought and how this sentiment impacts their future preferences.

Developing machine learning models that can handle Code-Switching (CS) presents a formidable obstacle in NLP. The vast majority of NLP resources, however, are not available in CS, which hinders their utility. Consequently, researchers have turned to data augmentation as a means of generating CS data by combining resources in other languages. Our research explores various strategies for improving the accuracy of NLP models by augmenting Arabic-English CS text. We replace non-CS words with corresponding CS lexicons to create augmented CS data. Unlike prior studies, we focus on the 'non-CS' variant as baseline data to ensure a controlled evaluation of our methods. Our results demonstrate the efficacy of different lexicons for data augmentation and the influence of varying mapping strategies on the performance of NLP models. We also provide various resources, such as code and integrated CS text, to facilitate future research in CS.

We show that any subgroup of homeomorphisms of a compact surface that fix the boundary, whose action within the surface's interior is highly transitive, cannot be topologically compact when using the compact-open topology's inherited structure.

We're investigating integrable boundary conditions for two related generalized backgrounds: torus branes and torus-like branes. These are derived from generalized deformations based on two supergroups. We provide a practical method for determining brane symmetry algebras, and use it to re-examine and discover new integrable branes in related theories. We've established correspondence with branes in related deformations and identified novel examples. We've also identified constraints for global brane behavior and discovered a connection between topological branes and global branes. This suggests that all topological branes can be represented as global branes, and we've identified a set of universal branes arising from a specific subalgebra within the symmetry algebra.

As hex-meshes' role becomes increasingly significant in computer graphics,
efficiently working with large, unstructured meshes becomes a pressing requirement.
To address this, we've developed the Tets/Hex algorithm, which effectively
addresses the challenge of the "overcrossing tetrahedron" issue in
unstructured meshes. By using the Tets/Hex algorithm, large mesh complexes
can be systematically simplified via a series of basic operations,
ultimately facilitating the development of high-level tools such as
system-level simplification and collision detection techniques.
In comparison to existing techniques, the Tets/Hex algorithm surpasses
the state-of-the-art by achieving a substantial 58% performance boost in
mesh complexity reduction and 53% improvement in overcrossing tetrahedron
removal compared to the previously established method of Tets/Inflations.
Furthermore, it surpasses the state-of-the-art tree-based method
(colincolin) by 41%, and offers a substantial speed advantage,
demonstrating a 3.5-fold speed increase in both collision detection and
mesh simplification tasks.

The tasks of relation extraction and knowledge graph link prediction share a
common link in their objectives, allowing them to complement each other in
the training process. Specifically, KGP link representation can facilitate
relation extraction, as it provides valuable guidance for identifying a link's
existing types, thereby narrowing down the potential correct type to a smaller
set. Furthermore, by applying KGP relation representation, link prediction's
type scores can be integrated as a regularizer for the type classification task
in the relation extraction process. By leveraging these two connections and
employing joint training, we achieve improved performance of both tasks, as
evidenced by the results of our extensive experiments.

This study introduces an innovative analytical delay model specifically tailored for deep submicron CMOS inverters. Developed based on the submicron inverter's transient voltage dynamics, the proposed model offers a closed-form analytical delay formula, which is computed using the Curve Fitting Toolbox in Matlab and subsequently verified through SPICE simulations.

To develop a universal smoothness assumption in reinforcement learning that applies across various settings, we take an original approach by mapping the states and actions of a MDP directly into a metric space, rather than using dimension-specific vector representations. This general framework allows us to establish a MDP smoothness condition based on this space mapping, and our contributions further show how certain value function approximations can effectively help us estimate the associated metric metric. Specifically, we introduce a metric learner inspired by neural tangent kernels that we prove converges to the true metric with a specific approximation error. As a result, we show that RTK-based approximations enable MDP-based RL algorithms to achieve performance on our new general smoothness condition, with the RTK-based approximation enabling access to the true metric at test time, thus allowing the model to accurately estimate value functions and action functions using standard FQ algorithms.

The ventral temporal cortex is crucial for recognizing objects, including distinguishing between living and non-living entities. While previous studies relied heavily on neuroimaging data that is often compromised by motion artifacts and resolution issues, high-density electrode recordings offer improved clarity. Our research utilized this high-quality data to explore the underlying principles of object recognition in the ventral temporal cortex. We found a complex pattern of neural activity where subregions respond selectively to different categories of stimuli, and our results suggest a functional hierarchy that combines localized and global processing areas to achieve accurate object recognition.

In scientific simulations, maintaining crucial characteristics such as convexity is of great importance. A new approach called the convex-closure filter has been developed to guarantee that the filtered simulation maintains its convexity. This concept was initially introduced by Z. Xu et al. in their 2015 study on preserving convexity in CFD data. Our implementation of the convex-closure filter is built upon the work of B. Welling and K. Glushenkov in their 2018 research on filtering multidimensional data. Our implementation leverages convex optimization to enhance computational efficiency, particularly when dealing with large datasets. Our testing demonstrates that the convex-closure filter effectively recovers the original data with a mean relative error of less than 5%, outperforming existing methods in accuracy and speed. Our approach offers a general and flexible framework for filtering simulations in various fields, including medical imaging, where preserving the convexity of structures is of great importance. Our research provides a starting point for a broader community to explore the applications of data filtering in preserving their characteristics.

Quasi-periodic oscillations type C, typically observed in low-hard and hard-intermediate states, have been extensively studied. Researchers have discovered a correlation between quasi-peripheral X-ray radiation and quasi-peripheral radio radiation, suggesting a possible connection between them. To investigate this relationship, a comprehensive analysis of X-ray and radio data was conducted for the atoll source MAX J1535-571 during a notable outburst in 2018. The results revealed a quasi-peripheral maximum intensity exhibiting an amplitude variation comparable to that of the peak intensity, indicating a possible connection. To determine the origin of this phenomenon, a detailed analysis of X-ray data was performed, revealing changes in a hot corona surrounding the accretion disc, which exhibited a temperature increase followed by a decrease as the source transitioned through a state boundary. Furthermore, a reprocessing analysis suggested an outer disc innering corresponding to a change from a high-temperature, high-corona state to a lower-temperature, lower-corona state. To further investigate this phenomenon, changes in the hot corona's height and electron density were calculated, which resulted in the outer disc innering corresponding to a change from a high-temperature, high-corona state to a lower-temperature, lower-corona state. To further confirm this phenomenon, changes in the hot corona's height and electron density were calculated, which revealed a correlation between the hot corona changes and the observed X-ray and radio data, indicating a possible connection

In the context of multi-agent reinforcement learning, coordinated training and testing can be challenging due to discrepancies between a model's performance derived from its own actions versus that of an unpredictable partner's. Our proposed solution centers on aligning the learning processes through coordinated data collection, utilizing an approach that leverages both self-generated and externally gathered data to promote cooperation. This strategy naturally enables models with different experiences to be compatible. Experiment results show that an ME-ML agent exhibits improved performance over its non-cooperative counterpart both in communication and collaboration.

We introduce a cutting-edge method for contrastive learning, which enables
one-shot recognition of materials in a scene, of materials within an image,
and even novel materials in an existing image. Our approach uses physics-based
rendering techniques and a straightforward loss function. We found that this
approach is easier to implement and can be scaled up faster than previous
methods. Notably, our results show that this method can also accurately
estimate material properties for known materials in new scenes.

Two equivalent formulations of Lie 2-algebras are recalled: one as a categorification of Lie algebras and another as 2-term L∞-algebras. The paper begins by defining strict 2-graded Lie algebras and their associated Lie 2-algebras. The Lie 2-algebra structure on the categorification of Lie algebras is then derived from this definition in a self-contained manner. Additionally various examples are provided to illustrate the different perspectives on Lie 2-algebras, including Lie 2-algebras arising from 2-Lie algebras, 2-ter Lie algebras, quadratic Lie algebras and Courant algebroids. Furthermore, Lie 2-algebras are shown to be related to 2-Courant algebroids. Finally, various applications of Lie 2-algebras are discussed, with an emphasis on their use in integrability and Poisson Lie groups.

We introduce a novel method for local image feature matching, where instead of a two-stage process, we directly model the relationship between image features as a dense pixel-to-pixel correspondence map. This approach, where local descriptors are learned in a descriptor-free manner, is based on the self-attention mechanism of the Transformer architecture, and is particularly effective for matching image regions with matching semantic content but varying scales and deformations. The significance of this approach is highlighted by the superior and state-of-the-art results it achieves on a variety of benchmarks, including the matching of both natural and synthetic images, where scale variations are present, and where no image detection is utilized. This work is also open-source.

This paper addresses the issue of bias in vector magnetic field measurements inferred from Stokes I and V spectra. Using synthetic data, we demonstrate that wave amplitude, wave direction, transverse magnetic field strength, and instrument signal-to-noise ratio affect the bias in inferred wave and magnetic field parameters. Notably, we identify four infrequently used but highly influential parameters. We effectively reduce bias in inferred parameters through a straightforward method of shifting inferred parameters by subtracting their mean value from initial inferred values. This method proves to be more reliable and efficient than traditional bias-reduction methods such as Monte Carlo simulations.

This research paper examines a real-world scenario in which consumers autonomously manage their energy needs by responding to a new, per-minute electricity tariff. The goal of each consumer is to minimize their total expenditure over the course of the month by utilizing energy management tools, such as scheduling energy demand and utilizing energy storage systems. The interaction among consumers is studied within a framework of an augmented game, with the aim of identifying the results that emerge when consumers strategically adjust their energy consumption to minimize costs. The game's characteristics are evaluated for its stability and equilibrium state. The findings are supported by a simulation study conducted in a representative neighborhood.

The generalized Rastall theory is employed to investigate the gravitational impact on the Hawking temperature and accretion disk formation around a charged black string within the Rastall framework. The results indicate that the effects of General Relativity are confined to the vicinity of the horizon, whereas those of the generalized theory manifest further away, particularly in the radial direction. These findings may hold significance for astronomical observations, which are generally conducted at distances far exceeding that of the accretion disk.

The results demonstrate that the power-law decay rates found in von Neumann's Ergodic Theorem for discrete systems directly correspond to pointwise scaling rates of a spectral measure with a spectral value of one. Moreover, assuming weak convergence, when no spectral gap is present, the convergence rates of the time-average in von Neumann's Ergodic Theorem rely on the shortest-time spectral measure tail.

The recent data from Gaia's Spectral Photometric photometers provide valuable insights into the properties of stars, including temperature, radius, and metallicity. A specialized analysis has been developed specifically for stars that are cooler than 5500 K. It involves applying cuts to ensure data reliability and adapting existing machine learning models to account for low-mass stars. This analysis is particularly effective for stars with a magnitude between 14 and 17, where it can accurately predict metallicity values with a standard deviation of approximately 0.1 dex. A key component of this analysis is applying additional cuts to eliminate interstellar absorption effects, which can distort spectra and affect predictions. It is observed that a certain threshold of interstellar absorption is more likely to occur in metal-rich stars. A thorough evaluation of the method's performance has been conducted, including tests on both data and 1700 stars with known metallicity values. This analysis has also identified recurring patterns of errors in metallicity predictions.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for determining the severity of global fire seasons based on existing satellite data. By combining Multivariate Proportional-To-Total (PTT) models and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithms, our analysis provides both historical and predictive insights into future fire seasons. Additionally, we propose a new severity index and calculate its global Severe Fire Season (SFS) duration, which indicates the period during which fire seasons are predicted to be severe.

We've conducted a thorough examination of eight distinct methods for evaluating the morphological intricacy of languages. These measures have two distinct applications: gaining insights into the characteristics of individual languages and enabling typologists to identify patterns across various languages. As these metrics often lack theoretical underpinnings, we seek to establish their reliability. To achieve this, we compare each measurement with relevant theoretical expectations. For instance, we anticipate that more morphologically complex languages should have greater vocabulary diversity, requiring less repetition. Additionally, we predict that languages with simpler word structures should be easier to process. We achieve this validation by statistically testing these hypotheses on a large collection of texts from 239 languages. Our study demonstrates that each measurement can be reliably correlated with theoretically based properties. However, we also note certain inconsistencies, suggesting that more research is needed to develop more robust metrics. Ultimately, we provide recommendations for developing more effective complexity measures.

Researchers investigating self-interacting dark matter have discovered an increased likelihood of lensing effects in galaxy clusters, particularly on small scales. These effects can be distinguished from those caused by cold dark matter due to their radial profiles and the shapes of the resulting images. Scientists have developed a unified framework for describing both types of lensing effects and have determined the constraints on dark matter self-interaction based on observed lensing events. These constraints are significantly tighter for infrequent events, with typical galaxy cluster encounters allowing for self-interaction cross-sections below 0.15 millipascal. Moreover, these interactions can serve as a means to estimate the dark matter mass within a galaxy cluster.

This research focuses on reducing the complexity of parametric partial differential equations (PPDEs) by finding an accurate approximation of the solution space using proper orthogonal decompositions (PODs) from limited data. A new optimization approach is proposed to maximize information gained from the equations and to select the most informative snapshots for generating reduced order models (ROMs). These models are used to predict solutions for new parameter sets with minimal complexity. The model is validated using a heat equation and demonstrated to significantly outperform traditional Gaussian process methods, while also reducing the need for snapshots and improving performance.

This research introduces the m-arcsinh kernel independent component analysis using
(I)NDE approach, where m-arcsinh kernel serves as the underlying kernel function.
Our proposed method offers a faster convergence rate compared to the m-ATAN2 kernel
used in previous studies, while also outperforming the tanh kernel approach in terms
of the established performance metrics. The m-arcsinh kernel ICADE method is
evaluated and shown to be more effective under various scenarios due to its better
inherent properties and adaptable kernel function design. The m-arcsinh kernel's
contribution and comparison to the m-ATAN2 kernel are thoroughly examined and
justified. The proposed method is supported by extensive simulations and real-world
data experiments demonstrating its superiority.

This study introduces an innovative approach for identifying time-location specific social media events occurring in real-time. Traditional event detection methods focus on offline analysis, requiring pre-collected data. Our real-time突发事件 detection model addresses this limitation by utilizing time-location social media activity as indicators and incorporates existing knowledge about recent events occurring in similar environments. Given the dynamic and diverse nature of emerging events, which cannot be fully captured using pre-defined event types, we introduce a novel data representation by splitting both data and knowledge streams into multiple 'eventualities,' enabling flexible inference across diverse event types. Our method combines local social media activity with global event history, represented as a multi-layered Bayesian network, to real-time突发事件 detection in a range of scenarios. Furthermore, our approach quantifies detection confidence, allowing event verification or refutation based on confidence scores. Empirical analysis confirms our method's efficacy, outperforming current state-of-the-art methods in various evaluation metrics.

We establish the optimal Lipschitz regularity of the trace for solutions to an elliptic problem defined on an open subset of R^N that includes the boundary of a given C^1, alpha-manifold embedded within it. The elliptic problem involves a surface measure applied to the manifold and variable coefficients. Our results also apply to a specific case of three-dimensional space and two-dimensional non-planar manifolds, relevant to a simplified model of a soap bubble's equilibrium state under an external force with variable density.

Advanced magnetic storage technologies rely on novel cobalt-based alloys with enhanced magnetic properties. This research investigates a wide range of cobalt-rich Y-C-B alloys using a generalised band structure method. For each cobalt variant, multiple samples were simulated to account for uncertainty. Using a computational simulation of natural processes, researchers identified stable compounds with a variety of cobalt concentrations. As cobalt content increases, predictions indicate a higher cobalt arrangement and decreased lattice size. Based on this analysis, certain alloys with intermediate cobalt concentrations, such as YCo$_{18}$B$_2$, YCo$_{21}$B$_4$, and YCo$_{22}$B$_5$, exhibit enhanced magnetic characteristics and are promising for magnetic storage. Furthermore, experimental results confirm a predicted high cobalt arrangement of three for the YCo$_{18}$B$_2$ alloy, demonstrating an unexpected enhancement in its magnetic properties.

This study addresses risk management for real-time bidding ad servers by developing an innovative approach that maximizes risk minimization under budget constraints. Our method utilizes a multi-armed bandit algorithm, which estimates the second moment of profit from display ads and identifies the optimal ad to display while managing risks efficiently.

Nonclassical properties in continuous-variable quantum systems are often marked by quantum correlations and Wigner negativity. This work's focus is on quantum states that exhibit Wigner negativity but no divisibility by the corresponding Gaussian state. We show that a family of states with Wigner negativity but no divisibility exists. Notably, we demonstrate that when one party holds an entangled state with Alice, there are specific measurement settings that can prove Wigner negativity to Bob, even if the state is not divisible. This implies that the presence of Wigner negativity as a resource can be identified through detection of quantum correlations, as the absence of quantum correlations for any Wigner-negative slicing scheme implies the need for no quantum storage. This finding is supported by a recent study that found no Wigner-negative slicing scheme exhibiting quantum correlations.

We used the finite-size quantum random access code capacity to develop a secure boundary for quantum key distribution (QKD) with a biased random seed in privacy amplification. Previous research assumed a perfectly random seed, but our work relaxes this condition to account for sample bias. Our secure boundary derivation is based on the quantum random access code, using the leak in the actual key as the leaked information. Numerical calculations showed that the secure boundary is consistent with the ideal case when the seed is perfectly random, but degrades when sample bias increases. However, the loss of secure key rate is relatively small when the bias is $b=0.875$.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new category, called the timelike (1,3)-Bertrand curve, is defined to fill this gap and its characteristics are identified. The properties of these 1-type Bertrand curves are also explored.

We'll examine the diffusion process described by the equation $u_t(t, x) = \frac{1}{2}V^2(x)u_{xx}(t, x) $ defined on a domain $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathbb{R}_+^d$, specifically the superprocesses introduced by Li (1989) at a branching boundary, the $\alpha$-stable superprocesses by Watson (2004) at the boundary of a Weyl $d$-polyhedron, and the super-Bessel processes by Mueller (1985) and Li (2010). The first step involves determining the manner in which paths of these processes approach the boundary. We demonstrate that there are distinct types of coalescence points and provide explicit conditions for their occurrence. We also establish conditions under which the distributions of specific functionals of the coalescence points are change of variable, which aid in simulating these processes and assessing gene genealogies. For the simplest scenario, we establish a general method to calculate expected functionals of coalescence points based on the solution structure. We also establish a change of variable for each type of coalescence point and employ it to derive a general expression for sampling distributions of specific subsets of lineages. These results have significant implications, including the emergence of a specific pattern of multiple mergers with exponent $\frac{2}{d+\alpha}$ and the derivation

In this work, we explore diagrammatic methods for analyzing the scattering behavior of individual and paired photons in a single-sided coupled QED system. We begin by establishing the foundational rules for constructing qED diagrams and demonstrate their application through an iterative construction process. Our findings reveal that these diagrams provide an effective framework for representing various many-body interactions between qED components, including a comprehensive analysis of their contribution to single- and multi-photon scattering processes. We derive an effective theory for describing multi-photon transmission in qED systems and utilize diagrammatic analysis to illustrate how local interactions give rise to long-range quantum correlations between qED components following multi-photon scattering. This framework not only facilitates the analysis of multi-photon scattering but also enables the examination of emerging phenomena, such as multi-photon entanglement, in complex qED networks.

A potential for dark matter models to produce a significant global signal from retreating DM nuclei in the Earth's atmosphere after collisions with high-speed particles has been identified. Specifically, dark matter models that have spin properties can create a distinct pattern in the accelerated section of the velocity curve. When DM has a particular characteristic spin, denoted by $\unicode{x2692}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\
This note employs Faulhaber's Formula to elucidate why odd Bernoulli numbers equate to zero.

Continuous phase modulation detection using conventional differential detection techniques is highly resistant to various channel disturbances, such as phase and Doppler shift. Its straightforward implementation, low system overhead, and simple transmitter design contribute to its popularity in short-range wireless communication systems. In this paper, we delve into the delay optimization of this detection technique for minimum mean square error and minimum mean square error with a differential component product decision function criteria. By employing a mathematical derivation based on Markov properties, we establish a condition for optimal delay and investigate how this optimal delay is affected by key factors such as data order and constant values. Our findings indicate that the optimal decision function remains robust against variations in system parameters and properties.
